At least 10 B-1 bombers used by the US military in the Iran conflict flew out of Fairford on Sunday, suggesting US officials were taking the threat seriously. Last week, five men in three vans near the military base were arrested, followed by a sixth British-Iranian national. All were released on bail, drawing criticism from the Pentagon. At the 2008 summit in Bucharest, Romania , German Chancellor Angela Merkel and French President Nicolas Sarkozy argued that they weren't ready to extend NATO membership to Ukraine. US President George W. Bush said he was in favor of having Ukraine enter into NATO. But both Germany and France said that that would hurt relations with Russian President Vladimir Putin. The NATO summit then decided that Ukraine would eventually join the alliance , but offered no timetable. At a press conference on Monday, Merz was asked about whether he thinks the time was right to talk about Ukraine's membership in NATO. To which Merz said, "If it [Ukraine] had become a member of NATO, this war could probably have been prevented." Merz meant Russia's war against Ukraine when he said "this war" at the press conference after a meeting with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte. Angela Merkel defended her decision at the Bucharest summit as of 2024 as well, saying a large proportion of the Ukrainian population had opposed joining NATO at the time.
